title: An idea becomes a connected system

scenes.title: The idea
scenes.purpose: Set up the single idea: the heading writes on, then the marker draws the light bulb and a terracotta wash fills it.
visuals: Cool pale grey-blue notebook paper with a faint dot grid (stationary)
Ink marker prop riding the live stroke end
Light-bulb contour, base lines, filament and rays in pressure-varied ink
Translucent terracotta wash that blooms inside the bulb

beats.development: Marker enters from below and writes 'an idea…' left to right.
Marker draws the bulb outline and its three base lines; the terracotta wash blooms inside, then the filament and rays tick on.

scenes.title: Connecting
scenes.purpose: Show the idea spreading into a system: each connector is drawn from the bulb outward, and each node outlines and fills with sage wash when its line arrives.
visuals: Six hand-drawn connectors, drawn in order
Five node blobs: ink contour, then an off-register sage wash
A closing link that turns the chain into a loop

beats.development: Connectors reach nodes one, two and three, and each node blooms when its line arrives.
Links to nodes four and five, then a closing link from node three makes a loop.

scenes.title: The system
scenes.purpose: Name the result, underline it in terracotta, then hold the finished drawing.
visuals: Caption written on directly on the paper

beats.development: Marker writes '…becomes a connected system', switches to terracotta for the underline, then leaves the frame.
Settled reading hold on the complete composition.

findings: One focus at a time: heading, then bulb, then the network spreading left to right, then the caption.
Connectors draw quickly (0.10–0.18 s each) so the system snaps together within the short preview. The wash blooms overlap the next connector as secondary actions.
Everything is settled by 2.70 s; the background and grain never move.
justifiedHolds: 2.70–3.00 s: final hold so the full caption and the network can be read together; the heading has been readable since 0.48 s.

notes: Scene-dependent palette refresh: cool notebook paper #E3E9EE replaces the earlier warm cream. Ink #343E42, terracotta #BC705A for the idea and emphasis, and sage #758D72 for the system nodes keep their semantic roles. Ink on paper contrast is about 8.96:1.

Construction learned from the source review: outline first, then a translucent wash confined to its shape; the marker tip rides the live stroke end; relationships are drawn after the objects; a dot-grid page for a systems topic. Source subjects, wording and branding are not copied.
Layered artwork with stroke-on reveals, not frame-by-frame redrawing.
Typography: @font-face local() declarations for Marker Felt, Chalkboard SE and Comic Sans MS. Scene drawing code is in scene.js; the GSAP timeline is built and registered inline in index.html.
Layer order: artwork canvas (bottom), marker canvas, then the DOM heading and caption on top.
